title: Quantifying Aerosolized Pollen Using a Handheld Air Particle Counter
author: Benjamin Lazarus
materials: Sample for a predefined and consistent duration.

steps.title: Prepare the Particle Counter
steps.instruction: Set up the device for sampling by attaching the filter and removing the nozzle.

substeps.instruction: Attach the manufacturer-supplied particle filter to the air intake.
Remove the sampling nozzle to reduce internal surfaces where pollen may adhere and to allow the sampling volume to be positioned closer to the air intake.

steps.title: Clear Internal Air Pathway
steps.instruction: Remove residual particles from the internal air pathway.

substeps.instruction: Run the particle counter for 60 seconds, or until zero particles are detected across all size bins.

steps.title: Configure Particle Size Bins
steps.instruction: Set the particle size bins to encompass the expected pollen grain size range.

substeps.instruction: Use the recommended binning scheme: 0.5–10 µm, 10–15 µm, 15–20 µm, 20–25 µm, 25–30 µm, and >30 µm.
If pollen size is known a priori, adjust bin boundaries to better match the expected pollen diameter distribution.

steps.title: Perform Baseline Measurement
steps.instruction: Establish a baseline in the absence of an active pollen source.

substeps.instruction: Place the particle counter at the intended sampling position.
Run the counter for the full sampling duration.
Confirm that particle counts above the pollen size threshold are negligible.

steps.title: Execute Pollen Sampling
steps.instruction: Position the device and record particle counts during the pollen event.

substeps.instruction: Position the particle counter intake at a fixed location relative to the airborne pollen source.
Ensure the intake is unobstructed and not in contact with any surfaces.
Ensure the air outlet remains unobstructed to maintain internal flow rate and avoid biasing counts.
Initiate sampling immediately before the expected presence of airborne pollen.
Record particle counts across all size bins.
Optionally record temperature and relative humidity if the device is equipped with integrated sensors.

steps.title: Quantify and Analyze Pollen Counts
steps.instruction: Calculate total pollen counts and evaluate the data for aggregation.

substeps.instruction: Estimate total pollen counts by summing particles exceeding a lower size threshold appropriate for pollen grains (commonly >10 µm).
Examine the proportion of particles detected in the largest size bin.
If oversized particles constitute a substantial fraction (indicating clumping/aggregation), apply a correction factor based on the mean number of pollen grains per aggregate.

steps.title: Maintain Consistency and Device Care
steps.instruction: Ensure reproducibility across measurements and maintain the device.

substeps.instruction: Maintain consistent sampling duration, intake positioning, and particle size binning.
Use identical device settings throughout the study.
Clean the device using the supplied filter between sampling sessions.

description: During extended sampling sessions, repeat background checks to ensure that airborne pollen or other particles are not accumulating in the surrounding air column.
